newsitem.title: USA: US OPTIONS FOCUS/Pros grow cautious, not investors.
newsitem.headline: US OPTIONS FOCUS/Pros grow cautious, not investors.

text.p: Some professional options dealers are growing increasingly cautious on the stock market as it continues to rally, but investors appear undaunted by the dazzling runup in stock prices.
"I don't see anybody coming in and doing too much protection," said one options dealer in Chicago. "We don't have a lot of people asking about that."
But he said personally he was recommending investors buy some index put options.
"All I can think of is buy puts," he said. "I have to go with the scenario that enough is enough."
The dealer said he expected the market to begin correcting early next week if a pullback does not begin after Friday's U.S. employment report for July is released.
He said he expected the blue chip Dow industrial average, which was up 87 points at about 8,262 in late trade Wednesday, to drop below 8,000 over the near term.
An index options trader at the Chicago Mercantile Exchange said many professionals were expecting a selloff soon and that even an in-line jobless report could touch it off.
"They're all looking to take this market and turn it around and sell it off," he said. "Everybody is looking at the downside right now."

Economists on average expect payroll employment to be up 193,000 in July compared to a 217,000 rate in June. The unemployment rate is expected to dip to 4.9 percent from 5.0 percent and average hourly earnings are forecast to rise 0.2 percent against at 0.3 percent climb in June.
The trader at the CME said implied volatilities in S&P 500 index futures options held firm, with August climbing about half a percentage point to 20.3 percent.
But in the S&P 100 index, volatilities were down on the day. The volatility index, which is calculated off certain front-month OEX options, was off 0.77, or 3.20 percent, at 23.27 in late trade.

The trader at the CME said most futures-options activity was from a British bank that was rolling some short calls to the 960 strike from the 950 strike. It was also actively trading several call spreads in both August and September.
"It's an active day with the unemployment report Friday," he said. "Everybody's getting jittery, especially at the highs here. It makes for a nice trading market."
But the options dealer said activity in the OEX and S&P 500 index was on the thin side.
"I haven't seen a lot of big orders," he said. "It seems like volume's down, but yet it hasn't been that bad."
At 1430 CDT/1930 GMT, overall OEX volume totaled 55,551 and SPX volume totaled 59,795 contracts.
